facts.text: Millersburg, Ohio, became the county seat of Holmes County in 1833, sparking a boom that saw ten stores, four taverns, and a printing office by that year.
The town’s original layout was drafted by Adam Johnson and Charles Miller in November 1815, with the first two homes built by James French and William Painter.
Historic Downtown Millersburg, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, invites visitors to stroll along streets that once hosted the first school and Presbyterian sermons.
The Holmes County Historical Society, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, preserves and archives the region’s rich history for future generations.
Millersburg sits 66 miles south of Cleveland, placing it in the heart of Ohio’s Amish Country and making it a hub for regional tourism.
The main east–west street of Millersburg was named Jackson, a nod to the town’s early civic planning.
